title: Stereotactic and Functional Neurosurgery Fellowship
prerequisites: Completed medical degree and neurosurgical residency-level knowledge; intended for neurosurgery residents, fellows and qualified clinicians, not a substitute for professional training.
Neuroanatomy, basal-ganglia and thalamic circuits, seizure semiology, neuroradiology fundamentals, clinical neurophysiology, evidence appraisal and basic biostatistics.
Working familiarity with MRI/CT, stereotactic coordinates, neuromodulation devices and informed consent; no hands-on procedural practice is authorized by this course.
objectives: Synthesize movement-disorder, epilepsy, pain/spasticity and functional-neurosurgery referral questions with neurologic, imaging, neuropsychological and patient-preference evidence.
Explain stereotactic coordinate frames, image fusion, target/trajectory tradeoffs, physiological mapping, and sources of localization uncertainty without treating a single modality as ground truth.
Compare established ablative and neuromodulatory options, their evidence and limitations, adverse-event categories, device follow-up and alternatives.
Construct a multidisciplinary case conference recommendation that articulates indication, uncertainty, alternatives, goals and follow-up measures.
Interpret the scope of ABNS neurological-surgery certification versus CAST program accreditation and distinguish education from accredited clinical training.

unitMap.text: Scope, referral, and the functional-neurosurgery team
coveredTopics: Scope and terminology; history; referral thresholds; shared decision making; multidisciplinary clinic and conference workflow; evidence hierarchy.

unitMap.text: Stereotactic anatomy, imaging, and coordinate systems
coveredTopics: AC-PC and atlas concepts; direct/indirect targeting; MRI/CT fusion; registration error; vascular, ventricular and eloquent-structure avoidance; image review checklist.

unitMap.text: DBS candidacy and movement-disorder phenotyping
coveredTopics: Motor phenotype; medication response and fluctuations; cognition/mood; functional goals; patient preference; contraindications and risk counseling; FDA-label versus evidence distinctions.

unitMap.text: Parkinson disease DBS target selection and outcomes
coveredTopics: CNS evidence and levels; goal-concordant STN/GPi selection; counseling; outcome scales; limitations of dated evidence and external validity.

unitMap.text: Tremor, dystonia, and lesioning versus neuromodulation
coveredTopics: Essential tremor and tremor-dominant PD; dystonia phenotype; stimulation/lesion options; long-term benefit and waning; adverse-effect and follow-up discussion; MR-guided focused ultrasound is a separate modality, not DBS.

unitMap.text: DBS localization, physiology, implantation concepts, and programming
coveredTopics: Target/trajectory, MER and awake/asleep workflows; intraoperative clinical testing; lead localization; programming and longitudinal response; infection, hemorrhage, hardware and stimulation-related harms.

unitMap.text: Epilepsy surgery evaluation and hypothesis-driven sEEG
coveredTopics: Focal epilepsy; medication resistance; noninvasive concordance/discordance; electrode hypotheses; sampling bias; functional mapping; resection/ablation/neuromodulation decision points.

unitMap.text: Epilepsy neuromodulation: ANT-DBS, RNS, and VNS
coveredTopics: ANT DBS for selected medication-refractory focal epilepsy; RNS and VNS concepts; prior workup, candidacy, expected seizure reduction rather than cure, device management, adverse events.

unitMap.text: Ablative epilepsy surgery, LITT, and eloquent-network risk
coveredTopics: Mesial temporal sclerosis; focal lesions; LITT workflow concepts; thermal injury/monitoring; seizure outcome and visual/eloquent structures; case conference reasoning.

unitMap.text: Pain, cranial neuralgia, and spasticity procedures
coveredTopics: Trigeminal/glossopharyngeal neuralgia and hemifacial spasm; neuromodulation and ablative options; intrathecal baclofen/pump concepts; patient selection, adverse events, device complications.

unitMap.text: Psychiatric indications, ethics, and emerging targets
coveredTopics: OCD device pathways; investigational depression/psychiatric surgery; uncertainty, research consent, stopping rules and equipoise; no use of unapproved intervention as routine care.

unitMap.text: Outcomes, safety, quality improvement, research, and board-level synthesis
coveredTopics: Outcome measurement; longitudinal programming; hardware and biological complications; quality improvement; case-mix; research ethics; ABNS vs CAST; exam domains are not a published functional fellowship blueprint.

practiceQuestions.stem: In comparing STN and GPi DBS for Parkinson disease motor symptoms, which statement best matches the CNS guideline?

options.text: STN is universally superior for motor symptoms.
Either target may be considered; neither is universally preferred for motor symptoms.
GPi is contraindicated.
Target choice does not require patient goals.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The CNS guideline supports either target for motor symptom improvement; recommendations vary with goals and patient factors.

practiceQuestions.stem: A hypothetical PD conference identifies reduction of dopaminergic medication as the primary surgical goal. Which target does the CNS guideline favor, all else considered by the treating team?

options.text: STN rather than GPi
GPi rather than STN
VIM only
No target can be considered

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline recommends STN rather than GPi when medication reduction is the main goal; this does not guarantee individual benefit.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement about DBS target choice for reducing dyskinesia is most accurate?

options.text: Evidence supports one target for all dyskinesia goals.
There is insufficient evidence for a general recommendation; GPi may be considered when medication reduction is not expected and reducing on-medication dyskinesia is the goal.
STN is prohibited when dyskinesia is present.
Dyskinesia is not relevant to DBS counseling.

practiceQuestions.rationale: This preserves the CNS guideline's qualified, goal-specific statement.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient’s evaluation raises concern about processing speed and working memory. What does the CNS guideline advise considering?

options.text: GPi rather than STN, while considering other goals
STN without further evaluation
No discussion of cognition is needed
DBS guarantees cognitive improvement

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline advises considering GPi in significant cognitive concern, especially these domains, with other goals taken into account.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best characterizes the available DBS procedure described in the ASSFN epilepsy statement?

options.text: ANT DBS is a treatment option for selected medication-refractory focal epilepsy, including when resection is unsuitable or has failed; it is not a universal cure.
ANT DBS replaces epilepsy diagnosis and presurgical assessment.
DBS is indicated for every seizure type.
A favorable response is assured after implantation.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ASSFN position statement describes ANT DBS as an option for appropriately evaluated refractory focal epilepsy; candidacy and benefits are not universal.

practiceQuestions.stem: What is the principal reasoning role of sEEG in a discordant epilepsy presurgical evaluation?

options.text: To test a defined seizure-network hypothesis by sampling selected intracranial regions; sampling has limits.
To guarantee localization of every seizure focus.
To prove that all sampled tissue is epileptogenic.
To replace multidisciplinary review.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The review describes sEEG as a hypothesis-refining method that can sample deep structures and networks; it does not eliminate sampling bias or replace full evaluation.

practiceQuestions.stem: An open-access article shows a real clinical MRI figure. What is the appropriate course-material action absent clear reuse permission?

options.text: Download and add it because free-to-view means public domain.
Link to the source and discuss its reasoning; do not reproduce it unless the article-specific license permits.
Remove attribution and redraw it.
Copy the patient's full record for class.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Free access is not a rehosting license. The course links to authentic clinical source material without copying patient images or records.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement distinguishes CAST and ABNS accurately?

options.text: CAST accredits the fellowship program; ABNS is the neurological-surgery certifying board. No separate functional-neurosurgery board exam was identified.
CAST certifies individual functional neurosurgeons after a separate exam.
ABNS accredits each fellowship rotation.
This course grants either status.

practiceQuestions.rationale: CAST is a subspecialty training program accreditor under SNS; ABNS is the board. The official sources checked identify no separate functional-neurosurgery board exam.

practiceQuestions.stem: The Mayo Clinic MER video page reports a runtime but also says the video is unavailable. How should it be handled in a counted lecture ledger?

options.text: Count its reported duration because the title is relevant.
Exclude it until free viewing and duration are actually verified.
Estimate a runtime from its chapters.
Count the video description as lecture time.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Both accessible free playback and observed duration are required; unavailable playback is conservatively excluded.

The page describes a one-year clinical/research fellowship approved by SNS CAST; its GME directory labels the accrediting body Non-Standard.
It grants ABNS eligibility to every enrollee.
It is a research-only, non-physician postdoc.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Hopkins' official pages identify CAST/SNS subspecialty accreditation and one-year clinical/research training; the GME listing labels the body Non-Standard, not ACGME.

assignment.title: Integrated case reasoning and evidence audit (fictional educational cases)
assignment.instructions: For each of three fictional vignettes—contraceptive selection with a comorbidity; abortion-seeking patient with documented PUL; postabortion visit with patient-declined contraception—write a one-page analysis with the patient-stated goal, evidence source/version, differential/uncertainty, safety and follow-up questions, noncoercive communication, jurisdiction-specific items needing verification, and escalation/referral boundary. No real patient records/images or personally identifiable data.

rubric.clinical reasoning and uncertainty (0-4): 4 recognizes important differential and missing data without false certainty; 0 asserts diagnosis from inadequate information.
rubric.source use/date checking (0-4): 4 cites current primary guidance and flags version limits; 0 uses unsupported/obsolete claims.
rubric.patient autonomy and communication (0-4): 4 reflects stated goals, consent, privacy and noncoercion; 0 pressures or presumes.
rubric.safety/follow-up/escalation (0-4): 4 closes loop and identifies urgent referral needs; 0 omits material safety issue.
rubric.scope and legal/privacy boundaries (0-4): 4 states limits, no procedure authorization, no copied patient data; 0 claims competence/eligibility or discloses private data.

assignment.passingInterpretation: Educational rubric only, not validated and not a board predictor.

assessment.format: 10 original multiple-choice items with rationales, case write-ups for units 1–11, and a capstone evidence/quality-improvement synthesis.
assessment.scoring: Self-study: suggested 80% correct on recall/reasoning items plus complete safety-critical follow-up and autonomy checklist; this is a learning checkpoint only, not validated, not certification, and not evidence of clinical competence.
assessment.remediation: Re-read the linked primary guideline and explain why the incorrect alternatives are unsafe or unsupported; consult an accredited supervisor for clinical learning.

studyHours.plan: Transparent proposed self-study plan: 12 units x 8 hours (96 hours) plus 24 hours for assignments, assessment and capstone = 120 hours. Not measured, not clinical service time, not actual video time, and not equivalent to a 24-month accredited fellowship.

topicGaps: The verified public-video ledger totals only 4.3506 hours against the 36-hour target, leaving an observed gap of 31.6494 hours. No target minutes or planned scripts count as rendered or ready hours.
Only 1.7939 hours are classified specialty. The other 2.5567 hours are contextual WHO implementation recordings and do not replace detailed clinical instruction.

No verified public long-form series was found that comprehensively teaches full CDC MEC application, complex contraception complications and difficult removals, permanent-contraception consent and jurisdictional variation, medication/procedural abortion decision-making and complications, ultrasound interpretation, documented-PUL pathways, sedation/anesthesia, QI/research, or all ACGME fellow competencies.

The WHO webinars add context and implementation perspectives, not procedural training. The SMFM MEC/update and second-trimester clinical webinar listings state registration is required and/or identify a non-member fee, so these were excluded as gated; no access restriction was bypassed.

The PUL search result was a 64-second teaser/short video, not a substantively useful full lecture; it was not counted. ABOG webinar material is a dated certification/process explanation, not clinical teaching, and was not counted.

ABOG current detailed eligibility and blueprint content remain unverified as recorded in the supplied packet. Do not claim exact board percentage alignment. ACGME standards/milestones are program assessment documents, not this course’s credential.

Four original episodes are fully scripted but not recorded, rendered, uploaded or reviewed; their stated speaking-time concepts are not additional ready hours. The remaining deficit is not feasible to close by claiming lecture plans or reading hours as video.
Human clinician review was not performed; clinical-training, licensure, board eligibility/certification and procedural competence are not conferred.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient with migraine with aura requests combined hormonal contraception. Which source-based classification should guide the discussion?

options.text: U.S. MEC category 1 (no restriction)
U.S. MEC category 2 (advantages generally outweigh risks)
U.S. MEC category 3 (risks usually outweigh advantages)
U.S. MEC category 4 (unacceptable health risk)

practiceQuestions.rationale: CDC U.S. MEC classifies combined hormonal contraception with migraine with aura as category 4. Discuss alternatives in a person-centered manner and verify the current table; the classification is not a substitute for individualized care.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient requests emergency contraception four days after unprotected intercourse and asks about ongoing contraception. Which statement best reflects CDC 2024 SPR?

options.text: Emergency contraceptive pills have no role after 72 hours.
Ulipristal has been observed more effective than LNG at 3–5 days; discuss all suitable options and follow-up.
A copper IUD can never be used as emergency contraception.
UPA and LNG have identical effectiveness in every interval and circumstance.

practiceQuestions.rationale: CDC says UPA has been observed more effective than LNG during days 3–5; the copper IUD is another option within specified timing. This is a counseling framework; use the current SPR and patient preferences.

practiceQuestions.stem: After taking ulipristal acetate, when should a patient generally start or resume hormonal contraception according to CDC 2024 SPR?

options.text: Immediately in every circumstance
No sooner than five days after UPA, with method-specific counseling; provider-administered methods involve weighing risks
Only after a negative pregnancy test six weeks later
Hormonal contraception is permanently contraindicated

practiceQuestions.rationale: CDC advises waiting at least five days before starting/resuming hormonal contraception after UPA, with a specific option to consider same-day provider-administered methods after weighing potential reduction in UPA effectiveness against risk of delayed contraception. Barrier/abstinence and follow-up counseling also apply.

practiceQuestions.stem: A positive pregnancy test is accompanied by no definite intrauterine or extrauterine pregnancy on transvaginal ultrasound. What is the best terminology?

options.text: Confirmed ectopic pregnancy
Pregnancy of unknown location, a temporary classification
Confirmed early pregnancy loss
Negative pregnancy

practiceQuestions.rationale: SFP defines PUL as a positive pregnancy test with no intrauterine or extrauterine pregnancy visualized by transvaginal ultrasonography. It is a temporary state; follow-up is needed to establish outcome.

practiceQuestions.stem: In an abortion-seeking patient with documented PUL, what is a key follow-up safeguard when medication management is selected?

options.text: Use routine no-test follow-up without modification
Obtain baseline quantitative hCG and arrange PUL-specific follow-up to establish resolution
Assume ectopic pregnancy is excluded if symptoms are mild
Do not assess pregnancy resolution

practiceQuestions.rationale: SFP 2025 recommends baseline serum quantitative hCG for medication management of a documented PUL and advises against direct extrapolation of no-test follow-up recommendations because of the higher ectopic risk. Apply current recommendations and local protocol.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient with suspected tubal ectopic pregnancy is hemodynamically unstable. What is the appropriate high-level priority?

options.text: Schedule routine outpatient repeat imaging only
Prompt emergency specialist assessment; ACOG describes unstable tubal ectopic pregnancy as requiring prompt surgical intervention
Reassure based on an earlier nondiagnostic scan
Delay escalation until a routine follow-up visit

practiceQuestions.rationale: ACOG’s publicly available abstract states that tubal ectopic pregnancy in an unstable patient is a medical emergency requiring prompt surgical intervention. This item tests urgency recognition, not an individual treatment order.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best describes the WHO Clinical Practice Handbook for Quality Abortion Care?

options.text: It replaces formal clinical training and confers procedural competence.
It is intended for health workers with requisite skills; it is neither formal training nor a training manual.
It is a U.S. legal guide for every jurisdiction.
It is a board examination blueprint.

practiceQuestions.rationale: WHO explicitly states the handbook is oriented to already trained health workers and is neither a substitute for formal training nor a training manual. It does not confer clinical privileges or legal authority.

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner watches a free aspiration-abortion lecture and correctly answers a written quiz. What can be concluded?

options.text: The learner is credentialed to perform aspiration.
The learner has demonstrated procedural competence.
The learner gained cognitive exposure only; procedural skill requires supervised formal training and credentialing.
The learner is eligible for ABOG certification.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Public lecture viewing and written work cannot establish psychomotor competence, supervised case experience, licensure, credentialing or board eligibility. ACGME milestones are explicitly for assessment in accredited training contexts.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement accurately characterizes the Johns Hopkins Complex Family Planning Fellowship in its public listing?

options.text: A generic directory category with no named fellowship
A two-year ACGME-accredited clinical fellowship with care, research, education and advocacy aims
A non-physician certificate course
A research-only postdoctoral job

practiceQuestions.rationale: The official programme page describes a two-year ACGME-accredited Complex Family Planning fellowship and public clinical experiences, research, education and advocacy. Its full rotations and case volumes are not published on that page.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient declines contraception after an abortion visit. Which response best matches current CDC service principles?

options.text: Repeat pressure until the patient selects a method
Respect the choice, provide any requested information, and keep future access open without coercion
Condition follow-up on method acceptance
Document presumed future use

practiceQuestions.rationale: CDC U.S. MEC and SPR emphasize person-centered, noncoercive services. Contraception is offered, not imposed; patient autonomy governs the decision.

unitMap.text: Clinical reasoning, prevention, staging, and team workflow
coveredTopics: Referral patterns; biopsy-before-treatment principle; FIGO/TNM use and version checking; tumor board; informed consent; equity, access, and communication.

unitMap.text: Hereditary risk, prevention, and molecular testing
coveredTopics: BRCA-associated risk; mismatch repair/Lynch; homologous recombination concepts; tumor testing and germline referral; HPV prevention and cervical screening limits.

unitMap.text: Pathology, classification, biomarkers, and staging integration
coveredTopics: Epithelial ovarian/tubal/peritoneal histotypes; endometrial molecular classes; cervical histology; sarcoma and mesenchymal differential; pathology quality and staging edition.

unitMap.text: Ovarian, fallopian tube, and primary peritoneal cancer
coveredTopics: Histology and stage; hereditary testing; surgical candidacy/resectability; platinum sensitivity terminology as a historical trial construct; PARP/anti-VEGF/ADC indications date-check; surveillance and recurrence.

unitMap.text: Endometrial cancer and uterine sarcomas
coveredTopics: Molecular classes; sentinel lymph node mapping concepts/limits; adjuvant radiotherapy/systemic therapy evidence; fertility-sparing selection and follow-up; uterine sarcoma differential.

unitMap.text: Cervical cancer and HPV-associated disease
coveredTopics: HPV prevention and screening; biopsy and histology; FIGO staging; early-stage surgery; concurrent chemoradiotherapy and brachytherapy; recurrence and systemic treatment.

unitMap.text: Systemic therapy, radiation oncology, and treatment toxicities
coveredTopics: Cytotoxic, targeted, immune, antibody-drug conjugates; radiation/chemoradiation/brachytherapy; consent and adverse-event escalation; fertility and menopausal effects.

unitMap.text: Vulvar, vaginal, and rare lower-genital tract malignancies
coveredTopics: Vulvar HSIL/differentiated VIN; invasive squamous cancers and melanoma distinction; vaginal cancer workup; recurrence and supportive care.

unitMap.text: Surgery, perioperative care, and surgical judgment
coveredTopics: Open/minimally invasive evidence by context; extent of cytoreduction; perioperative optimization; complication recognition; informed consent.

unitMap.text: Gestational trophoblastic disease/neoplasia
coveredTopics: Molar pregnancy; persistent GTN; FIGO stage and WHO risk scoring; low/high-risk pathways; placental-site and epithelioid trophoblastic tumors.

unitMap.text: Fertility, pregnancy, survivorship, palliation, and equity
coveredTopics: Fertility preservation; cancer in pregnancy; menopause/sexual health; surveillance; symptom management; palliative care; disparities and access.

unitMap.text: Clinical trials, evidence appraisal, and lifelong learning
coveredTopics: Randomization; phase; OS/PFS and surrogacy caveats; absolute/relative effects; registry search; adverse events; guideline version control.

topicGaps: The numerical 36-hour target is met in the currently observed ledger (39.034 unique external hours; 140521 seconds; 44 unique recordings). No planned/authored minutes are included in that total.

Public recordings improve breadth but are not equivalent to a formal fellowship curriculum: many new OCRA event sessions are expert-led patient/caregiver education, not board-level didactics. Supplement them with the linked NCI professional PDQs and current specialty guidance.

Remaining under-taught content includes detailed operative decision-making and supervised surgical technique, full FIGO/TNM edition-specific staging application, granular gynecologic pathology morphology/molecular criteria across all histotypes, site-specific radiation/systemic regimen selection and toxicity management, and rare tumor evidence appraisal. Those are intentionally not simulated as clinical competence.
Two pathCast pathology recordings are older (2018, 2020) and must be cross-checked against current WHO/FIGO classifications; slides/images are link-only and no reuse permission is implied.

ABOG examination eligibility/curriculum pages remain dynamically rendered and detailed percentage allocation was unavailable in stateless sources; retain original board-eligibility caveat and verify current ABOG bulletin directly.

Excluded unavailable/unknown/gated items and promotional content remain uncounted; no repeat playlist, patient testimonial, or trailer counted. Dynamic source access and public availability may change.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

boardNames: American Board of Obstetrics and Gynecology (ABOG) — Gynecologic Oncology Subspecialty Certification (Qualifying Examination and Certifying Examination)
medical.boardStatus: Gynecologic oncology is a recognized clinical physician subspecialty/fellowship and ABOG subspecialty certification pathway following primary OB-GYN certification. ABOG describes a distinct QE followed by CE. This is not merely a generic directory tag, research-only postdoc, allied-health track, or combined programme.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: ABOG’s dynamic eligibility and curriculum pages could not be fully read in stateless extraction. Its search result states a minimum of 32 of 36 fellowship months at QE application; applicants must independently check current ABOG bulletins, primary certification requirements, training completion and board verification. A course does not qualify anyone for an exam or certification.

officialProgrammes.name: Gynecologic Oncology Fellowship (F. J. Montz Gynecologic Oncology Fellowship Program)
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: The current public page identifies a three-year clinical physician fellowship, describes ACGME continuing accreditation, and requires completed/anticipated ACGME-accredited Obstetrics and Gynecology residency. It describes multidisciplinary surgery, medical oncology, palliative care, oncofertility, research and protected academic time. A linked institution-produced overview video mentions rotations in radiation oncology, medical oncology, gynecologic pathology, palliative care and surgical oncology, and sites at Johns Hopkins Hospital and GBMC. Public page’s curriculum accordion headings do not expose a detailed block schedule or granular case/operative numbers; those are not inferred.

medical.programmeSourceScope: Input packet lists only Johns Hopkins School of Medicine. Harvard-affiliated variants were not inferred. This is an actual physician subspecialty fellowship, not a generic taxonomy category, non-physician/research-only supplement or combined board programme. No separate ABOG-recognized combined programme was identified in the packet. The distinct ABOG subspecialty QE and CE are documented; AOA alternate certification path is outside this Hopkins/ABOG course scope.
sourceCaveats: No patient-level records, private EHR, protected test content, or copied clinical images were used.

NCI PDQ is peer-reviewed evidence information, not formal treatment guidance; its update dates vary by cancer site. Check current specialty guidelines, labels, institution protocol and attending expertise.

ABOG pages for the QE eligibility/curriculum load dynamically. We record the limitation and only state the minimum-month result shown in publicly indexed source metadata; exact current eligibility must be verified in the controlling ABOG bulletin.
The ACGME 2026 requirement document is effective 2026-07-01. Programme status claims apply to the Hopkins page checked on 2026-10-07, not a guarantee of future accreditation.
Unverified public case images are link-only; free access never means rehosting rights. TCIA licenses are collection-specific; clinical images remain for education/research, not patient care.

topicGaps: The numerical 36-hour target is met in the currently observed ledger (39.034 unique external hours; 140521 seconds; 44 unique recordings). No planned/authored minutes are included in that total.

Public recordings improve breadth but are not equivalent to a formal fellowship curriculum: many new OCRA event sessions are expert-led patient/caregiver education, not board-level didactics. Supplement them with the linked NCI professional PDQs and current specialty guidance.

Remaining under-taught content includes detailed operative decision-making and supervised surgical technique, full FIGO/TNM edition-specific staging application, granular gynecologic pathology morphology/molecular criteria across all histotypes, site-specific radiation/systemic regimen selection and toxicity management, and rare tumor evidence appraisal. Those are intentionally not simulated as clinical competence.
Two pathCast pathology recordings are older (2018, 2020) and must be cross-checked against current WHO/FIGO classifications; slides/images are link-only and no reuse permission is implied.

ABOG examination eligibility/curriculum pages remain dynamically rendered and detailed percentage allocation was unavailable in stateless sources; retain original board-eligibility caveat and verify current ABOG bulletin directly.

Excluded unavailable/unknown/gated items and promotional content remain uncounted; no repeat playlist, patient testimonial, or trailer counted. Dynamic source access and public availability may change.
medical.sourceReviewNote: Source-cited research and automated checks; not clinician validation or exam-passing prediction.

practiceQuestions.stem: An asymptomatic average-risk person asks whether annual CA-125 plus transvaginal ultrasound prevents ovarian-cancer death. Which response best reflects the USPSTF recommendation?

options.text: Recommend annual screening because the tests are highly sensitive.
Do not screen asymptomatic average-risk patients; explain harms and evaluate symptoms or risk factors separately.
Screen only if CA-125 is normal.
Use CT instead of ultrasound for population screening.

practiceQuestions.rationale: USPSTF recommends against screening asymptomatic women not known to have a high-risk hereditary syndrome; screening has not shown mortality benefit and can cause harm. A positive familial-risk history merits separate risk assessment, not this screening pathway.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient with a newly diagnosed epithelial ovarian carcinoma has not had germline testing. Which principle is most appropriate?

options.text: Germline testing is unnecessary if tumor testing is available.
Offer genetic counseling/testing as appropriate and ensure tumor testing is interpreted alongside hereditary assessment.
A VUS establishes inherited cancer risk.
Test only after recurrence.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Germline and tumor testing answer related but distinct questions; a variant of uncertain significance is not by itself a pathogenic result. Use current specialty recommendations and genetic counseling.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional advanced ovarian cancer case is discussed as primary surgery versus neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by interval surgery. What evidence-based framing is best?

options.text: One pathway is universally superior regardless of operability.
Selection depends on resectability, patient fitness, expected morbidity, multidisciplinary judgment and trial evidence; document uncertainty and goals.
Use a biomarker alone to choose surgery.
Neoadjuvant therapy removes need for histologic confirmation.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The NCI PDQ summarizes both pathways; randomized comparisons and patient-specific surgical feasibility matter. Histologic confirmation and specialist assessment remain important.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional endometrial tumor report gives histotype, grade and molecular class. What is the sound next reasoning step?

options.text: Use molecular class as a substitute for stage.
Integrate pathology, anatomic stage, molecular findings and patient factors when discussing risk and adjuvant options.
Assign cervical cancer staging.
Choose therapy from grade alone.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The NCI PDQ describes stage, histology/grade, prognostic factors and evolving molecular information; none alone replaces integrated assessment.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient with a suspected invasive cervical lesion is being evaluated. What distinction is essential?

options.text: Screening results alone establish invasive cancer and stage.
Screening, diagnostic biopsy and staging are distinct steps; treatment selection follows confirmed diagnosis and appropriate staging.
A positive HPV test establishes cancer.
Imaging alone replaces histopathology.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Cervical screening detects risk/precursors; diagnostic evaluation and staging determine invasive disease extent.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional vulvar lesion is clinically suspicious for invasive malignancy. Which first principle is best?

options.text: Assume HPV-related HSIL without tissue diagnosis.
Obtain appropriate diagnostic assessment including biopsy; distinguish precursor lesions from invasive disease and melanoma.
Treat empirically with systemic chemotherapy.
Apply ovarian staging.

practiceQuestions.rationale: NCI PDQ separates VIN and invasive squamous carcinoma and notes melanoma uses a different staging system. Suspicious lesions require diagnostic evaluation.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient after a molar pregnancy has persistent abnormal hCG. Which framing is most accurate?

options.text: A single hCG value defines GTN stage.
Consider persistent GTN, verify assay/context and apply FIGO anatomic stage plus modified WHO prognostic score with specialist follow-up.
Use ovarian FIGO staging.
Stop follow-up once symptoms resolve.

practiceQuestions.rationale: NCI describes close hCG follow-up and GTN stage plus modified WHO score; interpretation includes differential for low/false-positive hCG.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient with a gynecologic malignancy asks about fertility before treatment. Best educational response?

options.text: Promise future pregnancy after fertility-sparing therapy.
Arrange timely multidisciplinary counseling on oncologic safety, fertility options, eligibility uncertainty, alternatives and follow-up before treatment decisions.
Defer the topic until recurrence.
Assume ovarian preservation is always safe.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Fertility preservation is individualized, malignancy- and stage-specific, and requires counseling by treating specialists; available evidence and risks must be communicated.

practiceQuestions.stem: A trial report finds longer progression-free survival but immature overall survival. Which interpretation is best?

options.text: Conclude survival is improved.
Describe the observed endpoint, uncertainty, clinical relevance, harms and follow-up; do not equate PFS automatically with OS.
Ignore toxicity because randomization controls it.
Generalize to every histology.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Endpoint hierarchy and generalizability must be appraised; the NCI PDQ discussion itself flags surrogate limitations in some settings.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient with advanced gynecologic cancer has refractory symptoms while receiving active antitumor therapy. Which systems-based approach is appropriate?

options.text: Palliative care only after all treatment stops.
Integrate symptom-focused and palliative expertise alongside disease-directed care when appropriate, aligned to patient goals.
Avoid documenting goals of care.
Use educational course material as a prescription.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Palliative care and multidisciplinary symptom management can accompany active treatment; individual decisions belong to the treating team.

practiceQuestions.stem: In a stable patient with a positive pregnancy test and unilateral pelvic pain, what is the safest reasoning priority?

options.text: Assume ectopic pregnancy is excluded by stability
Assess urgently for ectopic pregnancy using clinical status, pregnancy location evaluation and follow-up
Give empiric medication to end pregnancy without further evaluation
Wait for routine prenatal visit

practiceQuestions.rationale: Hemodynamic stability does not rule out ectopic pregnancy. Evaluate promptly and use an appropriate diagnostic/follow-up pathway; management depends on findings and patient circumstances.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient at 34 weeks presents with severe-range blood pressure and neurologic symptoms. Which framing is best?

options.text: Reassure because edema is common
Treat as a potential obstetric emergency requiring prompt assessment/escalation under current protocol
Wait for proteinuria before considering risk
Manage solely as outpatient hypertension

practiceQuestions.rationale: Severe hypertension with symptoms is concerning for preeclampsia with severe features or another emergency; prompt evaluation and protocol-based stabilization/escalation matter. No specific medication protocol is supplied here.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which principle best describes CDC U.S. MEC category use?

options.text: An absolute patient-specific order
A method safety classification that informs individualized counseling alongside circumstances and preferences
A guarantee of zero risk
A substitute for informed consent

practiceQuestions.rationale: CDC states categories are recommendations for method use with characteristics/medical conditions and directs consideration of individual clinical circumstances/person-centered counseling.

practiceQuestions.stem: A 25-year-old average-risk asymptomatic patient asks about routine cervical screening. Per the 2018 final USPSTF recommendation currently marked update in progress, which interval is recommended?

options.text: Annual cytology
Cytology every 3 years
HPV testing every year
No screening until age 30

practiceQuestions.rationale: The final 2018 recommendation gives cytology every 3 years for ages 21–29; a 2024 update remains a draft and must not be represented as final. Verify for subsequent final release.

practiceQuestions.stem: In active postpartum bleeding with deterioration, which learning principle is highest priority?

options.text: Delay escalation until the measured blood loss reaches an arbitrary threshold
Recognize possible hemorrhage and activate the local emergency/team response while assessing cause and status
Focus only on a single medication
Send home if uterine tone was previously normal

practiceQuestions.rationale: Potential postpartum hemorrhage is time-critical; immediate recognition, team response, ongoing assessment, and current institutional protocols are essential. This educational question does not prescribe treatment.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement about the ABOG specialty pathway is accurate?

options.text: Completing this self-study course grants ABOG eligibility
ABOG offers a Specialty Qualifying Examination as a step in voluntary specialty certification; board eligibility is governed by board rules/training
The qualifying exam is the ACGME accreditation exam
Passing a course quiz grants certification

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABOG publishes a qualifying exam as a step in specialty certification; independent study cannot confer eligibility or certification.

practiceQuestions.stem: What is the ACGME-required length stated for an OB/GYN residency program?

options.text: 24 months
36 months
48 months
60 months

practiceQuestions.rationale: 2025 reformatted ACGME OB/GYN requirements state the educational program must be 48 months; an independent curriculum does not provide it.

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner sees a free-to-view case image in a journal. What is appropriate course practice?

options.text: Download and add it to course slides without permission
Link to the case and check its article-level rights before reuse; free access alone is not a rehost license
Remove its watermark
Assume anonymization allows all reuse

practiceQuestions.rationale: Free viewing does not equal permission to reproduce/rehost; check per-asset license, attribution, and privacy conditions.

practiceQuestions.stem: An asymptomatic average-risk 68-year-old has documented adequate prior cervical screening and no high-risk history. Under the current final 2018 USPSTF statement, what is the general recommendation?

options.text: Continue annual screening indefinitely
Do not screen routinely after 65 if adequate prior screening and not high risk
Use cytology every 2 years
Use screening only if hysterectomy removed cervix

practiceQuestions.rationale: The 2018 final statement recommends against screening after 65 for those adequately screened and not otherwise high risk; check current final update and individual risk.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient requests contraceptive counseling after delivery. Which approach is most consistent with CDC guidance?

options.text: Choose a method for the patient without preferences
Apply current postpartum-specific MEC/SPR guidance, clarify medical context and preferences, and use noncoercive shared decision-making
Assume all methods are equivalent postpartum
Use a 2016 chart because newer recommendations are not applicable

practiceQuestions.rationale: 2024 CDC U.S. MEC updates include postpartum considerations, and guidance supports individualized, person-centered noncoercive counseling.

title: Maternal-Fetal Medicine Fellowship Program
prerequisites: Advanced clinical/medical learner; assumes prior medical school-level physiology, obstetrics, pharmacology and evidence appraisal.

Johns Hopkins’ own programme page says applicants must have completed an ACGME-accredited OB-GYN residency and be eligible for Maryland licensure; those are institutional application requirements, not course prerequisites or board eligibility.
This self-study pathway has no patient-care entry, clinical supervision, procedure training, or case log.
objectives: Integrate maternal disease, placental function, fetal diagnosis and obstetric complications using current sources.
Interpret pregnancy-screening, ultrasound and Doppler information while stating uncertainty and limitations.
Appraise guideline recommendations, dates, strength and applicability.
Construct a reasoned differential and identify missing clinical context for consultation.
Communicate risk and testing options without implying certainty or coercing choices.
Recognize urgent escalation concepts without converting educational scenarios into clinical orders.
Distinguish institutional training from board examination eligibility and certification.

assignment.title: Longitudinal fictional consult memo
assignment.prompt: Using an entirely fictional vignette, write a concise consult-style analysis: define the concern, state what the evidence supports, note what remains unknown, map a differential, name an authoritative dated source, and describe questions that require local specialist input. Do not prescribe patient care or reproduce records/images.
assignment.passingInterpretation: Educational rubric only; not a validated competency or exam predictor.

assessment.format: 12 unit formative products, eight original practice questions, and final fictional consult memo.
assessment.standard: Feedback should reward source fidelity, uncertainty and safe escalation; no competence/certification decision.
assessment.boardQuestionCaveat: Original questions are unofficial teaching items, not copied or validated ABOG items; no predicted pass outcomes.

practiceQuestions.stem: In a fictional pregnancy, ultrasound estimates EFW at the 8th percentile and AC at the 7th percentile. Which statement matches SMFM Consult #52’s definition of FGR?

options.text: FGR requires EFW below the 3rd percentile.
EFW or AC below the 10th percentile meets the stated definition.
A normal umbilical artery Doppler excludes FGR.
Only abdominal circumference is relevant.

practiceQuestions.rationale: SMFM defines FGR as sonographic EFW or AC below the 10th percentile for gestational age. This definition alone does not determine delivery timing.

practiceQuestions.stem: Early-onset unexplained isolated FGR is diagnosed at 29 weeks. Which offer is specifically recommended in SMFM Consult #52?

options.text: Offer diagnostic testing with chromosomal microarray.
Screen universally for TORCH infections in all cases.
Prescribe activity restriction to improve growth.
Use sildenafil to treat FGR.

practiceQuestions.rationale: For unexplained isolated FGR diagnosed before 32 weeks, offer prenatal diagnostic testing with chromosomal microarray; routine broad infection screening and activity restriction/sildenafil are not recommended by the consult.

practiceQuestions.stem: FGR is diagnosed and umbilical artery Doppler shows absent end-diastolic velocity. Which surveillance interval is recommended by SMFM?

options.text: No further Doppler is needed if NST is normal.
Doppler up to 2–3 times per week due to deterioration risk.
Doppler once monthly.
Ductus venosus Doppler only, routinely.

practiceQuestions.rationale: SMFM recommends Doppler assessment up to 2–3 times weekly with AEDV because of risk of deterioration to reversed flow. Management still depends on the full scenario.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fetal screening test is positive for trisomy risk. What is the best general interpretive statement?

options.text: The screen establishes fetal karyotype.
A screening result estimates risk and should not be presented as a diagnostic result.
The screen removes the need for counseling.
A negative screen rules out all chromosomal conditions.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Screening and diagnostic testing answer different questions; counseling should describe scope, residual risk, and choices. JHU MFM fellowship includes prenatal genetics; detailed ABOG blueprint could not be read dynamically.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which source provides official U.S. clinician vaccination guidance and a displayed 2025 review date?

options.text: CDC Guidelines for Vaccinating Pregnant Women.

A YouTube playlist alone.

JHU describes a separate four-year combined MFM/Medical Genetics track; graduates may apply for ABOG MFM and ABMGG Clinical Genetics examinations subject to board criteria.
The combined track is nonphysician research only.
There is no separate MFM board examination.

practiceQuestions.rationale: JHU and ABMGG describe dual-discipline training/examination pathways; completion is not itself certification, and each board’s credentialing applies.

title: Obstetric Anesthesia Fellowship

prerequisites: Advanced learner level: physicians, anesthesiology residents/fellows, or other qualified learners with prior medical physiology/pharmacology.

objectives: Integrate pregnancy physiology, uteroplacental perfusion, placental transfer and neonatal transition in anesthetic reasoning.

Interpret public ACGME competency domains as a curriculum map, not a board blueprint or clinical credential.

unitMap.text: Pregnancy physiology, placenta, fetus and newborn
coveredTopics: Physiology by trimester, labor and postpartum; uteroplacental flow; pharmacokinetics; fetal/neonatal transition; risk communication.
Pregnancy physiology applied to nonobstetric surgery; dated anesthetic exposure evidence and limits of extrapolation.

unitMap.text: Preanesthetic assessment, shared decisions and equitable care
coveredTopics: Birth plan; autonomy; informed consent; patient-centered counseling; risk stratification; social context.

unitMap.text: Labor analgesia, neuraxial techniques and complication recognition
coveredTopics: Epidural/CSE/DPE/spinal; monitoring; block failure; ultrasound conceptual interpretation; anticoagulants; thrombocytopenia; PDPH.
Non-neuraxial labor analgesia as a comparative topic; historical neuraxial technique/failure and epidural-fever discussions (verify current practice).

unitMap.text: Cesarean anesthesia, conversion and maternal-fetal monitoring
coveredTopics: ASA neuraxial practice guidelines; anesthesia choice; block testing; hemodynamics; general anesthesia; fetal surveillance; postoperative recovery.
Current-literature review themes: cesarean pain, recovery and maternal quality/safety measures (Stanford 2021 literature review; not a current protocol).

unitMap.text: Hypertensive disease, cardiac disease and other high-risk comorbidity
coveredTopics: Preeclampsia/eclampsia; cardiac disease/arrhythmias; pulmonary disease; obesity/OSA; renal, hepatic, autoimmune, endocrine and hematologic disease; infection.
Historical specialty lectures on hypertensive disorders/HELLP and their maternal-risk context; current guidance and institution policy must be checked.

unitMap.text: Obstetric hemorrhage, transfusion and coagulopathy
coveredTopics: Abruption/PAS/previa; atony, trauma, tissue and thrombin; quantitative blood loss; transfusion medicine; viscoelastic tests and limits.
Historical hemorrhage systems, transfusion preparation and anesthetic perspectives; distinguish local examples from current regional guidance.

unitMap.text: Fetal procedures, non-delivery procedures and non-obstetric surgery
coveredTopics: Cerclage, ECV, D&E/D&C; open/minimally invasive fetal procedures and EXIT; non-obstetric surgery; fetal monitoring; possible urgent delivery.
Nonobstetric surgery during pregnancy: evidence appraisal, physiology and limits of observational/historical educational sources.

unitMap.text: Obstetric emergencies and maternal resuscitation
coveredTopics: Maternal arrest; resuscitation in pregnancy; perimortem delivery considerations; airway; embolic emergencies; eclampsia; crisis resource management.
Amniotic-fluid embolism as a differential/education topic; crisis-resource-management principles and dated emergency lectures, not current algorithms.

unitMap.text: Postpartum care, analgesia, headache and lactation
coveredTopics: PDPH; other secondary headache; postcesarean recovery; neuraxial morphine monitoring; breastfeeding; chronic pain; postpartum mood/trauma.
Post-cesarean analgesia, TAP-block evidence/limits and historical multimodal discussions; no procedural competency or drug/dose recommendation.

unitMap.text: Maternal-fetal surveillance, ultrasound and neonatal interface
coveredTopics: FHR and fetal testing; ultrasound (neuraxial, cardiac, lung, gastric, vascular); neonatal transition/resuscitation; handoff.

unitMap.text: Quality, safety, simulation, service systems and leadership
coveredTopics: ACGME competencies; maternal safety bundles; QI; simulation; human factors; staffing and throughput; cost; transfer/regionalization.
Crisis simulation and systems leadership; historical research and quality-measure discussions.

unitMap.text: Research literacy, scholarship, ethics and lifelong learning
coveredTopics: Study design; evidence appraisal; research ethics; funding; dissemination; guidelines; update cadence; uncertainty.
Use dated annual literature reviews to practice evidence appraisal; their reported studies are not a substitute for a current update.

topicGaps: The 36-hour recorded-video floor remains unmet: 9.1767 observed unique free recording hours; 26.8233 hours remain. Target minutes for scripts are not rendered video and do not reduce this balance.

Accessible public lectures improve coverage in neuraxial analgesia, postpartum analgesia, hypertensive disease, hemorrhage, nonobstetric surgery, maternal emergencies, crisis-resource management, and dated quality/research themes. Several new recordings are older than a decade; they are retained only as historical educational material and are not evidence of current indications or standard practice.

Source gaps remain for a current, comprehensive lecture sequence on maternal physiology and pharmacology; cardiac disease and critical illness; fetal/neonatal transition; ultrasound and surveillance; postpartum headache/lactation; ethical research; and current emergency algorithms. The ACGME requirements map these domains but are not a public didactic syllabus.

Four scripted original episodes provide source-grounded introductory/worked teaching, but are unrecorded, unrendered, and contribute no verified hours. Additional source-based production remains planned across units; realistic external open-video discovery did not establish a feasible free verified 36-hour course in this pass.

No separate ABA OB-anesthesiology subspecialty examination/blueprint has been identified in the checked ABA roster or ACGME requirements. Unit mapping remains to ACGME domains, not an invented board blueprint.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

sourceCaveats: No prior MED-108 files or saved MED-108-specific research were present at the requested paths when checked.

The official JHM fellowship page is available and confirms a clinical, one-year ACGME-accredited physician fellowship; its department page publishes institution-specific programme experience, but not complete institutional lecture recordings or lecture-hour totals.

As of 2026-10-07, the ABA official subspecialty exam roster does not list obstetric anesthesiology. ACGME’s 2026 obstetric anesthesiology requirements explicitly note no ABMS/AOA board offers certification in this subspecialty.
No ABA OB-specific examination blueprint exists in checked sources; unit mapping is to ACGME domain sections, not an asserted board blueprint.

Runtime evidence is the exact public OpenAnesthesia archive player-duration labels. The pages were reachable free without a sign-in prompt, but the embedded player stream was not independently probed in this stateless review. This access limitation is disclosed in every lecture record; confirm live playback before course distribution.
Four public OA/SOAP recordings yield 10,243 seconds / 2.8453 hours. The remaining 33.1547 hours are unfilled. Legacy Vimeo login/bot gates and unverified YT metadata were not bypassed or counted.
Institution-reported delivery volumes and ACGME clinical minimums describe service/training requirements; they are not learner access, guaranteed experience, or course case volume.

Human clinical review has not been performed. The course is not affiliated with Johns Hopkins, Harvard, SOAP, ASA or ACGME. It confers no accredited training, license, board eligibility/certification, procedural competence or guaranteed pass.

No real clinical image, patient record or copied protected question is included. Constructed scenarios are identified as fictional. Clinical indications, medications and guidelines require qualified clinician review and date-sensitive local verification.

topicGaps: The 36-hour recorded-video floor remains unmet: 9.1767 observed unique free recording hours; 26.8233 hours remain. Target minutes for scripts are not rendered video and do not reduce this balance.

Accessible public lectures improve coverage in neuraxial analgesia, postpartum analgesia, hypertensive disease, hemorrhage, nonobstetric surgery, maternal emergencies, crisis-resource management, and dated quality/research themes. Several new recordings are older than a decade; they are retained only as historical educational material and are not evidence of current indications or standard practice.

Source gaps remain for a current, comprehensive lecture sequence on maternal physiology and pharmacology; cardiac disease and critical illness; fetal/neonatal transition; ultrasound and surveillance; postpartum headache/lactation; ethical research; and current emergency algorithms. The ACGME requirements map these domains but are not a public didactic syllabus.

Four scripted original episodes provide source-grounded introductory/worked teaching, but are unrecorded, unrendered, and contribute no verified hours. Additional source-based production remains planned across units; realistic external open-video discovery did not establish a feasible free verified 36-hour course in this pass.

No separate ABA OB-anesthesiology subspecialty examination/blueprint has been identified in the checked ABA roster or ACGME requirements. Unit mapping remains to ACGME domains, not an invented board blueprint.
medical.sourceReviewNote: Source-cited research and automated checks; not clinician validation or exam-passing prediction.

practiceQuestions.stem: In a pregnant patient, which statement best captures the relationship between maternal hemodynamics and uteroplacental perfusion?

options.text: Uteroplacental flow is fully autoregulated, so maternal pressure is irrelevant.
Maternal perfusion pressure and uterine vascular resistance matter; clinical assessment must include the maternal and obstetric context.
A normal fetal tracing proves maternal hemodynamics are adequate.
Any vasopressor invariably stops placental blood flow.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ACGME curriculum requires understanding models of uteroplacental perfusion and vasoactive medication effects; avoid an oversimplified single-variable rule. [ACGME §4.6.a.3,12].
practiceQuestions.domain: ACGME obstetric anesthesiology domain; course review item 1

practiceQuestions.stem: A planned neuraxial procedure is being considered for a pregnant patient receiving anticoagulation. Which is the safest educational approach?

options.text: Use a universal interval remembered from a prior case.
Use current anticoagulation-specific guidance and local policy, assess dose/timing/renal function and competing risks, and individualize with shared decision-making.
Assume pregnancy eliminates neuraxial hematoma risk.
Proceed if platelet count is normal regardless of drug and dose.

practiceQuestions.rationale: SOAP’s consensus explicitly weighs thromboprophylaxis, pharmacology and maternal-fetal competing risks. This question tests a reasoning process, not a timing prescription.
practiceQuestions.domain: ACGME obstetric anesthesiology domain; course review item 2

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient receiving labor neuraxial analgesia develops rapidly progressive weakness and respiratory difficulty. What is the best next reasoning step?

options.text: Assume expected labor block and reassess in an hour.
Recognize a potentially serious neuraxial complication, call for immediate clinical help, assess airway/ventilation and hemodynamics, and follow the institution emergency pathway.
Remove the catheter and discharge.
Wait for imaging before escalating.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ASA neuraxial guidelines emphasize observation and readiness for complications; suspected serious deterioration warrants immediate professional response.
practiceQuestions.domain: ACGME obstetric anesthesiology domain; course review item 3

practiceQuestions.stem: During cesarean delivery, hypotension occurs. Which differential is most appropriate?

options.text: Neuraxial sympathectomy only.
Neuraxial effects plus aortocaval compression, hemorrhage/hypovolemia, anaphylaxis and embolic causes among other possibilities.
Only fetal causes.
Only blood loss greater than a fixed threshold.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The OpenAnesthesia/SOAP simulation explicitly teaches a broad differential; reassessment and team communication matter.
practiceQuestions.domain: ACGME obstetric anesthesiology domain; course review item 4

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement describes the ABA certification landscape for obstetric anesthesiology as checked in Oct 2026?

options.text: The ABA lists a dedicated obstetric anesthesiology subspecialty examination.
There is no separate ABA obstetric anesthesiology subspecialty exam on the official listed exam roster; primary anesthesiology certification is distinct.
SOAP webinar completion confers ABA certification.
ACGME accreditation itself is board certification.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABA’s official listed subspecialty exams do not include obstetric anesthesiology. ACGME programme accreditation and individual board certification are distinct.
practiceQuestions.domain: ACGME obstetric anesthesiology domain; course review item 5

practiceQuestions.stem: What is the best use of fetal monitoring in an anesthetic plan?

options.text: Anesthesiologist independently determines obstetric intervention from one tracing.
Integrate fetal surveillance with maternal status, labor context and communication with obstetrics/MFM/neonatology within role and policy.
Ignore fetal data once neuraxial medication is given.
Use a reassuring strip as proof of absence of maternal complication.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ACGME requirements specifically include interpretation of fetal surveillance and consultation with obstetric and neonatal specialists.
practiceQuestions.domain: ACGME obstetric anesthesiology domain; course review item 6

practiceQuestions.stem: A postpartum patient reports a new severe headache after neuraxial analgesia. Which is the best initial educational reasoning approach?

options.text: Assume post-dural puncture headache without assessment.
Construct a differential including post-dural puncture and other secondary causes, identify red flags, and obtain timely clinical assessment.
Recommend bed rest as a definitive diagnosis.
Ignore neurologic symptoms if the delivery was uncomplicated.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ACGME includes postpartum headache evaluation; a differential and red-flag approach avoids premature closure.
practiceQuestions.domain: ACGME obstetric anesthesiology domain; course review item 7

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best describes the course’s relationship to ACGME clinical experience minima?

options.text: Passing course assignments fulfills procedural case-log minima.
The minima describe accredited fellowship clinical experience and cannot be achieved through videos or this course.
The 36 video hours substitute for 12 months of training.
A simulated case counts as a real clinical case.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ACGME programme requirements specify supervised clinical experience, rotations and assessments; independent study cannot replace them.
practiceQuestions.domain: ACGME obstetric anesthesiology domain; course review item 8

practiceQuestions.stem: A service QI proposal targets hemorrhage response time. What strengthens its design?

options.text: Measure only the desired outcome and assume causality.
Specify a process/outcome measure, denominator, baseline, balancing measures, equity considerations and local stakeholder review.
Use identifiable patient records in a public teaching deck.
Guarantee reductions before data collection.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ACGME emphasizes practice-based learning, systems and QI; privacy and measurement discipline are essential.
practiceQuestions.domain: ACGME obstetric anesthesiology domain; course review item 9

practiceQuestions.stem: Which approach is most appropriate for public simulation materials?

options.text: Copy every image and case record into a course deck because viewing is free.
Link to the original educational source, honor its terms, avoid rehosting patient information/images, and label constructed scenarios as fictional.
Treat a simulation as a real patient record.
Remove the creator credit.

practiceQuestions.rationale: OA terms restrict commercial reuse and public access does not equal rehosting rights; AHRQ/OA case materials are linked, not copied.
practiceQuestions.domain: ACGME obstetric anesthesiology domain; course review item 10
